title: How to Grill Sliced Apricots for a Gourmet Summer Side
meta_description: Discover how to grill sliced apricots on a BBQ mat for a sweet, caramelized summer side. Step-by-step tips, flavor combos, and cleanup tricks for perfect result
html:
Grilling sliced apricots on a BBQ mat transforms a simple fruit into a caramel‑kissed side that pairs beautifully with grilled chicken, pork, or a fresh salad. The non‑stick surface of a BBQ Grill Mats protects delicate fruit from flare‑ups while giving you those signature grill marks. Follow these practical steps, and you’ll have a gourmet‑worthy apricot garnish ready in minutes.

Why Use a Grill Mat for Apricots?

Apricots are soft and high in natural sugars, so they can stick or burn when placed directly on a hot grill grate. A BBQ Grill Mats provides a smooth, reusable surface that distributes heat evenly, preventing the fruit from slipping through the grates and eliminating flare‑ups caused by dripping juices. The result is a gentle sear that caramelizes the fruit without turning it to mush.

Preparing the Apricots

Start with fresh, ripe apricots. Look for fruit that yields gently to pressure but isn’t mushy. Here’s a quick prep routine:

  1. Rinse the apricots under cool water and pat dry.
  2. Slice each apricot in half lengthwise, then remove the pit.
  3. Cut the halves into ¼‑inch thick slices. Thinner slices cook faster and develop more grill marks.
  4. In a shallow bowl, toss the slices with a light coating of olive oil, a pinch of sea salt, and optional flavor boosters such as a drizzle of honey, a sprinkle of fresh thyme, or a dash of smoked paprika.

The oil helps the fruit release its sugars onto the grill mat, while the seasoning adds depth without overpowering the apricot’s natural flavor.

Setting Up Your Grill and Mat

Preheat your gas or charcoal grill to medium‑high (about 400‑450°F). While the grill heats, lay the BBQ Grill Mats directly onto the grates. The mats heat up quickly—usually within 2–3 minutes—so they’re ready when the fruit is.

Tip: If you’re using a charcoal grill, arrange the coals for indirect heat and place the mat over the cooler side. This method prevents the apricots from cooking too fast and gives you more control over caramelization.

Grilling the Sliced Apricots

Once the mat is hot, arrange the apricot slices in a single layer, leaving a little space between each piece. Close the lid and grill for 2–3 minutes per side. You’ll see nice grill lines and a glossy, caramelized surface. Flip the slices only once; excessive handling can cause them to break apart.

If you like a touch of smoky flavor, add a few wood chips to the coals or use a smoker box. The apricots will pick up a subtle smokiness without becoming bitter.

Finishing Touches and Serving Ideas

When the apricots are lightly charred and tender, remove them from the mat and let them rest for a minute. The residual heat will finish the cooking process.

Here are three quick ways to turn grilled apricots into a standout side:

  • Apricot & Arugula Salad: Toss the warm slices with peppery arugula, crumbled goat cheese, toasted almonds, and a drizzle of balsamic reduction.
  • Grilled Apricot Salsa: Combine chopped apricots with diced red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime juice. Serve alongside grilled fish or chicken.
  • Apricot Glaze for Meats: Puree the grilled apricots with a splash of white wine and a pinch of salt. Brush the glaze onto pork chops or turkey during the final minutes of cooking.

All of these ideas benefit from the clean, non‑sticky surface of the BBQ Grill Mats, which makes cleanup as easy as a quick wipe.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your Grill Mat

After the grill cools, scrape off any food residue with a silicone spatula. Wash the mat in warm, soapy water or place it on the top rack of your dishwasher. Once dry, store it flat or rolled in a dry place. Proper care ensures the mat stays non‑stick for many summer seasons.

FAQ

Can I use the grill mat for other fruits?

Absolutely. The same mat works great for peaches, pineapples, and even watermelon cubes. Just adjust cooking times based on thickness.

Do I need to oil the mat before grilling apricots?

No. The apricots are already tossed in a thin oil coating, which prevents sticking. The mat’s non‑stick surface is designed to work without additional grease.

Is the grill mat safe for high‑heat cooking?

Yes. BBQ Grill Mats are made from heat‑resistant silicone that can handle temperatures well above typical grilling ranges, so you can safely sear steaks or vegetables on the same mat.
